title: Google put AI chips in orbit

beats: Google just launched four AI chips into orbit.
Real hardware. Circling Earth right now.
October first. A SpaceX rocket, out of California.
Sixty-one minutes later, the satellite was loose in orbit.
Google says everything works.
Why? AI is running out of power.
The same week, Amazon locked up six hundred ninety megawatts of nuclear. For twenty years.
Space has a trick.
In the right orbit, the sun almost never sets.
Refrigerator-sized. Four chips. About one kilowatt of solar power.
A test, on purpose.
Before launch, Google hit the chips with a proton beam.
They survived more radiation than a five-year mission delivers.
The real plan: eighty-one satellites, one kilometer wide, six hundred fifty kilometers up.
Working like one computer.
The math: launch must fall to about two hundred dollars a kilo.
Then a kilowatt in orbit costs about eight hundred ten dollars a year. Like Earth's power bill.
Google's guess: twenty thirty-five.
The catch? No air in space. Heat can only radiate away.
So this isn't a data center yet. It's a survival test.
Over the coming weeks, Google gathers data on radiation, heat and speed.
That decides if the other eighty go up.
Would you trust your AI to a satellite?
Follow for what the data says.
